core_obligations: Set up the induction on the number of irreducible components using the affineness criterion, and suppose given an affine open U handling the first r-1 components together with an affine open V of the r-th component containing T cap Z_r (proof lines 9094-9107).

Show that Delta = (U cap Z_r) setminus (U cap V) is closed in U and contains no element of T, and use prime avoidance to find a standard open U' of U containing T cap U and avoiding Delta, so that U' cap Z_r lies in U cap V (proof lines 9108-9118).

Repeat the same argument for Delta' = (U cap (Z_1 union ... union Z_{r-1})) setminus (U cap V) to make the other intersections closed as well, completing the induction up to line 9135 (proof lines 9121-9135).
proof_roadmap: Induct on the number of irreducible components.
Use prime avoidance to make the intersection with the current component lie inside the chosen affine open.
Repeat symmetrically for the already handled components.
difficulty_reason: The lemma assembles the per-component affine containment hypotheses into a single affine open containing the whole finite set T. The proof proceeds by induction on the number of irreducible components: given an affine open U meeting the first r-1 components in the desired way and an affine open V inside the r-th component containing T cap Z_r, one shows that Delta = (U cap Z_r) minus (U cap V) is closed in U and contains no point of T, and then uses prime avoidance to replace U by a standard open U' containing T cap U and disjoint from Delta, so that U cap V becomes closed in U; a symmetric argument handles the remaining components (proof lines 9094-9135). H2: the two prime-avoidance steps that make the intersections closed are the substance.
